title: Don't Light Churches On Fire And Shoot People To Death
subtitle: Advice to a shaken nation
body_html:
As I'm writing, I'm watching a press briefing that I'd rather not be watching. I have some direct things to say about it.

Earlier today, in the state of Michigan, somebody decided to set a church on fire. They did that so that people would run out, and they could shoot them to death.

At least four people are dead:

Authorities say a gunman rammed a vehicle through the front of the church during a large service, began shooting and then intentionally set a fire that grew into a large blaze. Police believe they may still find victims in the burned-out building.

To this murderer, I say: f- all the way off, all the way to hell. I know his name, and I’m not going to share it, because no one should remember who you are. This is best practice in the case of mass shootings:

Scholarly research suggests that the media can potentially impact the prevalence of mass shootings in two respects: (i) some individuals may be inspired to mimic the actions of highly publicized offenders; and (ii) a more general contagion process may manifest as a temporary increase in the likelihood of shootings associated with a triggering event.1

This was a Mormon church. My heart goes out to all those injured and all those who will be grieving in the aftermath of this loss.

To those considering becoming gunmen, arsonists, and mass murderers? No one's gonna remember who you are either. There are too many of these events. Now, it's no way to get remembered; no one will remember you, or the horrible things you thought about doing.

On the off chance that somebody thinks about you more than one moment, they're gonna remember you as a loser, for maybe a second, and then forget you ever existed when the next loser does something obnoxious and not worth remembering.

Please, consider doing something nice. People might remember that. If you want to go out in a blaze of glory? Do it serving humanity, not subverting it. Help other people in a moment when they need it. And consider living! You know, to see what happens next, to see what happens when you love somebody, and do something that sacrifices your good for the good of others. There are a lot of options that are not murder, that are loving, that are caring, that are supportive, and that may lead anybody to remember your name!

If you're thinking of burning a church to the ground, don't. If you're thinking of shooting people, for your own glory, don't. Don't be a loser. Don't be a vampire. Be somebody you'd want in your life. Be somebody you'd want in the lives of people you care about. Be better than the world you hate now, be better than those who hurt you, be better than those who broke the ones you loved, and be better than the worst devils among us.

Be better, don't be worse. That's advice, directed to every potential gunman, every day you go, without becoming an actual gunman, that's a good day, and you can be proud of it.

Share

Subscribe now

To everyone suffering right now, I'm so sorry. I hope you find peace.

1

Fox, J.A., Sanders, N.E., Fridel, E.E., Duwe, G. and Rocque, M., 2021. The contagion of mass shootings: The interdependence of large-scale massacres and mass media coverage. Statistics and Public Policy, 8(1), pp.53-66.
